newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Tap's Woollybutt well has 11-17m column.
newsitem.headline: Tap's Woollybutt well has 11-17m column.

text.p: Tap Oil NL said on Monday that the Woollybutt One exploration well off the Western Australian coast near Barrow Island was likely to contain a gross hydrocarbon column of betweeen 11 and 17 metres.
The company said one repeat formation test on the well recovered about 10 litres of 48.2 degree API oil.
It said the operator planned to run seven inch lining in preparation for production testing the well.
Tap Oil said that since April 24 the partners had completed a wireline logging suite, a rotary and percussion sidewall coring programme, and three Repeat Formation Tests (RFT).

"Preliminary analysis of the above-mentioned programme indicates the presence of a gross hydrocarbon column within the objective Barrow Group reservoir of a minimum of 11 metres, and up to 17 metres," it said.
"One RFT was able to recover formation fluids, being approximately 10 litres of 48.2 degree API oil."
Tap Oil has a 10 percent stake in the well, which is operated by 20 percent owner Mobil Exploration & Producing Australia Pty Ltd.
Pan Canadian Petroleum International Ltd also has 40 percent while Hardy Petroleum Ltd has 30 percent.
